BiblicalUsage: Rabab is to shoot an arrow. Jacob said of Joseph, 'The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him'; and David sang that the LORD 'sent out his arrows, and scattered them; and he shot out lightnings, and discomfited them.'
TheologicalSignificance: My conviction is that the two shootings belong together: men shot at Joseph, and God shoots at Joseph's enemies — the arrows change hands, and the hated one is kept.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; King David
